plain.text: While Apollos was in Corinth, Paul came to Ephesus and found some disciples. He asked, "Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?" They said, "We have not even heard that there is a Holy Spirit." They had received John's baptism. Paul explained that John's baptism was a baptism of repentance, telling people to believe in the one coming after him, Jesus. They were baptised in the name of the Lord Jesus. When Paul placed his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they spoke in tongues and prophesied. There were about twelve men.

Paul spoke boldly in the synagogue for three months about God's kingdom. When some refused to believe and spoke evil of "the Way", he took the disciples and held daily discussions in the lecture hall of Tyrannus for two years, so that everyone in the province of Asia heard the word of the Lord. God did extraordinary miracles through Paul; even handkerchiefs and aprons that had touched him were taken to the sick, and they were healed.

Some Jews who went around driving out evil spirits tried to use the name of Jesus: "In the name of the Jesus whom Paul preaches, I command you to come out." Seven sons of Sceva did this. The evil spirit answered, "Jesus I know, and Paul I know about, but who are you?" The man with the spirit attacked them, and they ran out naked and bleeding. Everyone in Ephesus was seized with fear, and the name of the Lord Jesus was held in high honour. Many believers openly confessed what they had done. Those who had practised sorcery brought their scrolls and burned them publicly; their value was huge. In this way the word of the Lord spread widely and grew in power.

Paul decided to go to Jerusalem, and then to Rome. About that time a great disturbance arose in Ephesus. Demetrius, a silversmith who made silver shrines of the goddess Artemis, gathered the craftsmen. Paul's teaching that gods made by hands are not gods at all was hurting their business, and the temple of Artemis might lose its greatness. They were furious and shouted, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!" The whole city was in uproar. People rushed into the theatre, dragging Paul's companions. Paul wanted to appear, but the disciples would not let him. Most of the crowd did not even know why they were there. For two hours they shouted. Finally the city clerk quieted them. He said the men had not robbed temples or blasphemed their goddess, and any complaint should be settled in the proper courts. They were in danger of being charged with rioting. Then he dismissed the assembly.

summary.bigIdea: In Ephesus the message about Jesus spreads with power, changing lives and even shaking the business of idol-making.
points: Disciples who knew only John's baptism receive the Holy Spirit.
People who practised magic burn their scrolls; the word of the Lord grows in power.
Silversmiths start a riot, but the city clerk calms the crowd.
summary.reflection: New believers in Ephesus gave up things that were harmful to them. Is there something you sense God asking you to let go of?
